owler: One who owls; esp., one who conveys contraband goods. See Owling, n. [Obs. or Prov. Eng.] T. Brown.
owlery: An abode or a haunt of owls.
owe: 1. To possess; to have, as the rightful owner; to own. (old) Thou dost here usurp The name thou ow'st not. Shak. 2. To have or possess, as something derived or bestowed; to be obliged to ascribe (something to some source); to be indebted or obliged for; as, he owed his wealth to his father; he owed his victoty to his lieutenants. Milton.
owing: 1. Had or held under obligation of paying; due. There is more owing her than is paid. Shak. 2. Had or experienced as a consequence, result, issue, etc.; ascribable; -- with to; as, misfortunes are often owing to vices; his failure was owing to speculations.
ownership: The state of being an owner; the right to own; exclusive right of possession; legal or just claim or title; proprietorship.
owling: The offense of transporting wool or sheep out of England contrary to the statute formerly existing. Blackstone.
owelty: Equality; -- sometimes written ovelty and ovealty. Burrill.
owl: 1. (Zoöl.) Any cpecies of raptorial birds of the family Strigidæ. They have large eyes and ears, and a conspicuous circle of feathers around each eye. They are mostly nocturnal in their habits. | 1. To pry about; to prowl. [Prov. Eng.] 2. To carry wool or sheep out of England. (old) Note: This was formerly illegal, and was done chiefly by night. 3. Hence, to carry on any contraband trade.
owner: One who owns; a rightful proprietor; one who has the legal or rightful title, whether he is the possessor or not. Shak.
owlish: Resembling, or characteristic of, an owl.
own: To grant; to acknowledge; to admit to be true; to confess; to recognize in a particular character; as, we own that we have forfeited your love. The wakeful bloodhound rose, and shook his hide owns. | Belonging to; belonging exclusively or especially to; peculiar; -- most frequently following a possessive pronoun, as my, our, thy, your, his, her, its, their, in order to emphasize or intensify the…
owher: Anywhere. (old) "If he found owher a good fellow." Chaucer.
owenite: A follower of Robert Owen, who tried to reorganize society on a socialistic basis, and established an industrial community on the Clyde, Scotland, and, later, a similar one in Indiana.
owlet: A small owl; especially, the European species (Athene noctua), and the California flammulated owlet (Megascops flammeolus). Owlet moth (Zoöl.), any noctuid moth.
